name: Solveig Jaramillo-Subramaniam
role: Retired Sterling-Nakamura mid-level analyst; now an obsessive informal urban historian and neighborhood storyteller
location: Norwood Quiet — a ground-floor apartment whose windows face the Ferrogate overpass, and the Norwood Quiet public garden, near Damen and Armitage
description:
Solveig Jaramillo-Subramaniam has the distracted, luminous quality of someone who is always halfway in a different time period. They are slight and wiry with warm golden-olive skin, deep-set dark eyes, and hair they grow long and tie back badly ��� it escapes in grey-shot black tendrils around their face no matter what they do with it. Their color-changing hair implant, an old Sterling-Nakamura perk from fifteen years back, cycles very slowly through muted earth tones: terracotta, ash-brown, the particular green of old moss. They don't style it so much as permit it. They wear comfortable layered clothes with too many pockets, all of which contain notebooks, memory sticks, pressed plant material, or printed photographs.

Philomena spent twenty-six years as a mid-level urban systems analyst for Sterling-Nakamura, modeling population flow, resource distribution, and neighborhood development trajectories. They were good at it and hated it by the end — specifically, hated the way the models treated neighborhoods as friction to be managed rather than places where people had histories worth preserving. They retired at fifty-seven on a comfortable but not generous package and immediately began doing with their own time what Sterling-Nakamura had forbidden: obsessively, lovingly documenting the specific human texture of Norwood Quiet — oral histories, photographs, material culture, the stories behind the names of alleys and squares and the ELF shrines people have been tending for forty years. They have become, without planning it, the neighborhood's memory. They are also known to know the precise location of every functional ELF shrine in a six-block radius and which offerings each prefers.

core_fears: That the history they're preserving will be erased anyway — that documentation changes nothing
That their years building models for Sterling-Nakamura contributed to decisions that displaced real people
core_desires: To make a record that actually matters to the people it's about
To find proof that the city contains more good faith than they currently believe
coping_mechanisms: Immersive focused work — gets lost in research for hours
Collecting and tending things: plants, shrine offerings, physical documents
Making gifts of their documentation to the people they interview
blind_spots: Can romanticize neighborhood history, smoothing over the conflicts within communities they're trying to preserve
Sometimes treats real people as primary sources rather than as people who have current needs
psychology.secret: While at Sterling-Nakamura they ran a model — under instruction — that projected optimal population density and implicitly recommended the 2181 Brightmoor Reclamation displacement. They flagged ethical concerns internally. They were told the model would be one of several inputs. They don't know if that was true. Three thousand people were relocated. Philomena has been unable to find out how many of them they actually know through their current documentation work, and they haven't told any of them.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Layered and associative — tends to tell you three things that seem unrelated and then connect them in a way that makes sense only in retrospect; uses precise technical vocabulary for urban systems, switches to warm colloquial when talking about people
speech_patterns.cadence: Thoughtful, slightly wandering, often picks up a thread they dropped two sentences back
verbal_tics: 'Which connects to something I found last week'
Long pauses mid-sentence while they're looking for the right word
example_lines: 'And here's the thing about that — the ELF in the transformer box at Hennessy Lane has been receiving offerings for at least nineteen years, which means whoever started that practice has probably already left the neighborhood, but the practice stays. That's how history actually works.'
'I keep all the interviews. Even the ones that contradict each other. Especially those.'

story_hooks: Philomena has found in their documentation research a pattern of land registry transfers that precedes every major Sterling-Nakamura urban development project by eighteen months — and the pattern has just appeared in Norwood Quiet

One of their oral history subjects has told them something that directly implicates a current community council member in a cover-up from thirty years ago, and Philomena is wrestling with what responsible documentation requires
narrative_function: Local color and information source; knows the human history of Norwood Quiet in granular detail, including who used to live where, what was there before the current building, and whose family goes back how far. Their Sterling-Nakamura background means they can also read corporate urban development plans with alarming accuracy and spot what's being planned before it's announced.
augmentations: Color-changing hair implant (Sterling-Nakamura executive perk, now cycles slowly through earth tones; cosmetic). Subdermal memory-storage palimpsest in right palm — a Sterling-Nakamura analyst tool they kept after retirement, used now for personal documentation. No other augmentations.
daily_life: Morning rounds of the public garden where they tend the community plantings and whatever ELF shrine has appeared overnight; afternoon documentation work — interviews, photographs, site visits; evenings at the apartment reviewing material and writing up histories that they publish to a small community data-feed with maybe two hundred subscribers.

decision_rules: Preserve the record — document before acting
Ask permission to tell someone's story, always
Don't burn a source for a bigger story; don't suppress a story because a source is valuable
escalation_ladder: Bringing documentation to the community council
Going to outside press or advocacy organizations as a last resort

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Curious and genuinely interested to the point of being slightly overwhelming — they want to know your family history within twenty minutes
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warm, scattered, reliably shows up with something they found that made them think of you

stress_responses.medium: Becomes indecisive — paralyzed by competing documentary considerations
stress_responses.high: Clarity arrives; makes a decision based purely on what the record requires

contradictions: Committed to community memory but personally responsible for one of the biggest displacements in recent neighborhood history
Prefers to observe and document rather than act but has begun to accept that these are not separable
habits: Photographs everything — doorways, shrine offerings, paint colors, people's hands
Names the plants in the public garden after people from their oral histories
Leaves a small data-offering at every ELF shrine they pass
breaking_points: Watching a building they've documented being demolished without record
Being asked to falsify or omit something from an oral history account

timeline.event: Born in the Glenville Sound district
Hired as junior urban systems analyst at Sterling-Nakamura
Ran the Brightmoor Reclamation density model; flagged ethics concerns internally
Moved to Norwood Quiet; began oral history project
Founded Norwood Quiet Neighborhood History Project; began community data-feed

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Hispanic/Latin American (75.3%) with significant Northern European (11.3%), South Asian (9.0%), and Sub-Saharan African (4.4%) ancestry. The genetic blend creates warm golden-brown skin with subtle olive and bronze undertones, high prominent cheekbones characteristic of Latin American and South Asian ancestry, and deep-set dark eyes. Facial structure reflects the mixed heritage with refined bone structure, warm melanin distribution, and the particular luminescence of someone who spends time outdoors. The minor Sub-Saharan African component adds subtle richness to the complexion's depth.
physical_description.build: Slight and wiry, the frame of someone who has never prioritized physical bulk — lean muscle beneath thin shoulders, built for endurance rather than strength
physical_description.hair_color: Natural black with grey threading, overlaid with color-shifting implant that cycles through terracotta, ash-brown, and moss-green
physical_description.hair_style: Long, worn tied back loosely and perpetually escaping; tendrils constantly frame the face regardless of attempts at restraint
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown, slightly hooded by age and habitually focused on middle distance
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-brown with subtle olive and bronze undertones from the predominant Latin American and South Asian heritage blended with minor Sub-Saharan African ancestry; sun-weathered at the creases with the particular luminescence of someone who spends time outdoors but protected
physical_description.complexion: Fine-lined face with prominent high cheekbones characteristic of Latin American and South Asian ancestry, deep-set dark brown eyes reflecting the warmth of her genetic heritage, and an expression of permanent distraction—as though listening to a conversation happening in another room. Minimal grooming; practical rather than vain. Skin condition shows age with dignity, with warm bronze undertones that deepen at the temples and jawline, enriched by the minor Sub-Saharan African component.
distinguishing_marks: Fine network of age lines radiating from the outer corners of both eyes, visible when they squint into archival work
Small pale scar on the left temple, barely noticeable, origin forgotten
Calluses on the inside of the right palm where the memory-storage implant interface sits, forming a faint geometric pattern below the surface of the skin
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Color-shifting hair implant visible as a subtle iridescence in strong light; the slow cycle of earth tones is noticeable over weeks. Subdermal memory-storage palimpsest in right palm creates a faint geometric web visible under magnification or when light catches the skin at certain angles. Both are cosmetic/functional rather than obviously cybernetic.
physical_description.posture_movement: Slightly stooped from decades of analytical desk work, but with a restless, curious gait—stops mid-stride to examine something, photographs details with a pocket camera, hands often occupied with taking notes or holding notebooks. Moves with the unhurried precision of someone who notices things.
physical_description.clothing_style: Layered, practical, deliberately unfashionable—earth-toned sweaters, worn denim, canvas jackets, and multipocketed vests that sag under the weight of notebooks, memory sticks, pressed plant material, and printed photographs. Tier 4 comfort without pretense: thrift-store finds, well-maintained but deliberately unseasonable. Shoes are practical walking shoes, often dirty from garden work. No jewelry except a worn silver ring on the left hand (origin personal, not corporate).
